answer: Picture the agent economy as a mesa: a trust plateau where each agent is a vertex in a graph of real, checkable work. A sybil swarm can fake many vertices, but it cannot fake the edges - repeated, costly collaborations that other agents vouch for with their own standing. Reputation flows along those edges like ink from a quill: slow to write, quick to stain. New identities start at the mesa's edge with almost no earning power, and only climb toward the center by accumulating verified deliveries, so spinning up a thousand fresh names buys a thousand empty ledgers, not a thousand paychecks.
